panelDocTopBar.about: The document top bar: on the left the document's current state (who last edited it, offline, read-only); on the right the people online, suggestions, comments, ask the AI teammate about the whole doc, and '...'.

s1.name: Someone edited it
s1.note: Left says the editor's name and '... editing'; clicking it opens the history; a row of online avatars on the right.

s2.name: Offline
s2.note: The left switches to 'Not connected; changes sync when reconnected', not 'who edited it'.

s3.name: Read-only
s3.note: No edit permission: a single 'Read-only' on the left, no toggling back to editable.

s4.name: Suggesting
s4.note: Someone who can edit switches to Suggesting: what they type becomes suggestions, and the bar counts them.

s5.name: A mentor opens it
s5.note: Someone who can only suggest stays in Suggesting with no switch; hovering says who accepts.

panelDocOutline.about: The document outline: headings in the body listed indented by level; clicking one scrolls to that section; an empty state when there are no headings.

s1.name: Has headings
s1.note: Three heading levels, each indented one step; clicking emits its pos.

s2.name: No headings yet
s2.note: No heading in the body at all: shows an empty-state line, not a blank box that won't open.

panelDocPresence.about: The 'who's here' on the top bar: avatars of others with this doc open; people are round, AI teammates square; more than four collapse to '+N'.

s1.name: A room full
s1.note: Six people, first four drawn, the other two collapse to '+2'. One person with two tabs counts once.

s2.name: One person
s2.note: Only one person here draws a single face, no '+N'.

panelDocEditButton.about: The button used on the small cards and strips inside a document: default, the single primary action in a group (solid), and disabled.

s1.name: Default
s1.note: Light fill with an outline, a card's secondary action.

s2.name: Primary
s2.note: One solid fill; only one per group, since accept and accept-all can be on screen together.

s3.name: Disabled
s3.note: Unclickable while busy or without permission.

panelDocFindBar.about: The in-document find bar: input, which match of how many, previous/next, close; says 'No matches' when nothing matches.

s1.name: Has matches
s1.note: Five matches found, sitting on the 2nd.

s2.name: Nothing found
s2.note: The query matched nothing.

panelDocSlashMenu.about: The Notion-style slash-menu overlay: type '/' in the body to pop it up; lists block types; the keyboard walks the list, the mouse can click too.

s1.name: A list
s1.note: The block-type list that pops up when you type '/' at a line start: icon, name, a hint on the right; the row the keyboard rests on is highlighted.

panelDocOverlays.about: The pieces that sit over the body and follow it: the selection toolbar, the slash-menu overlay, the code-block toolbar, the block handle. Each computes its own position, since none is part of the body.

s1.name: Slash menu open
s1.note: 'Where the menu opens' is decided above; this only draws: a block-type overlay pinned near the cursor.

panelDocBubble.about: The bar that floats over selected text: AI teammate, comment, plus block styles, several text formats and link when editable; when not editable the formats become 'Copy'. On phones it becomes the bar above the keyboard.

s1.name: Editable
s1.note: Editable: 'Cheese' and 'Comment' on the left, then block style, bold/italic/strikethrough/inline code/highlight, three status tags, link.

s2.name: Not editable
s2.note: Read-only collapses the formats, leaving just 'Copy'; it's greyed when nothing is selected.

s3.name: Inside a status tag
s3.note: Cursor inside a status tag: only 'Yes / No / At risk' and 'Remove', no formats.

s4.name: The phone bar
s4.note: On phones it sits above the keyboard: with nothing selected, AI teammate and comment are disabled; formats target the text to be typed at the cursor; undo and redo are added at the end (this cell uses the editor with an undo stack).

panelDocLinkCallout.about: The overlay that adds, edits or removes a link on selected text. Its position is computed to sit next to those characters.

s1.name: Enter URL
s1.note: Selected text not linked yet: an empty URL input with save and cancel. Saving adds the link to those characters. The catalog shows the overlay in normal document flow (position: static), not anchored to a real selection.

panelDocVersionDiff.about: The right column of the change history: the selected version compared with the one before it, which paragraphs changed — added paragraphs green, removed red with strikethrough, changed ones marking the added/removed characters inline.

s1.name: Several paragraphs changed
s1.note: A line up top says how many paragraphs were added/removed/changed; below, one block per paragraph.

s2.name: Same as the previous version
s2.note: No changes between the two versions: only the top line and a 'No changes' line remain.

panelDocHistory.about: The change-history dialog: every version on the left (newest on top); on the right, by default what changed since the previous one, switchable to that version's full text; when editable you can restore to that version.

s1.name: Several versions
s1.note: Four versions loaded, the newest selected, the right side showing its diff against the previous one.

s2.name: No versions yet
s2.note: Not a single version: the right side shows an empty-state line.

panelDocAgentResult.about: The card after the input is handed off: queued, editing or answering (all stoppable); when done editing it says how many spots changed, undoable, can keep going; an answer is the answer itself, convertible to a comment.

s1.name: Queued
s1.note: It's busy: says 'Auto-reply when idle', offers only 'Cancel'.

s2.name: Editing
s2.note: Editing this doc: says 'Editing...', offers 'Stop'.

s3.name: Done editing
s3.note: Done: says how many spots changed, offers 'Undo', and 'Keep editing' below.

s4.name: Undone
s4.note: After undo it can be restored.

s5.name: Answered
s5.note: The answer is read as Markdown: convertible to a comment, can follow up.

s6.name: Nothing found
s6.note: Asked, and it has nothing to add: shows 'No issues found'.

panelDocAgentBox.about: The input that opens when you click the AI teammate: an input on top, typeable on open; below, common phrasings in two groups, 'Edit' and 'Ask', filtering as you type.

s1.name: Edit a selection
s1.note: A passage selected: the 'Edit' group first (polish, shorten, to list/table, translate), then 'Ask'.

s2.name: Ask about the whole doc
s2.note: For the whole doc: only the 'Ask' group (summarise key points, review the whole doc, suggest structure).

s3.name: Read-only, ask only
s3.note: When not editable only 'Ask' remains: the input placeholder becomes 'Enter a question'.

panelDocSuggestionStrip.about: The strip above the body: how many edit suggestions the AI teammate has left, previous/next, decide all at once; when all are handled it says how many were accepted and rejected.

s1.name: Some left
s1.note: Three left: previous/next, plus 'Reject all / Accept all'.

s2.name: All handled
s2.note: Done: says two accepted, one rejected, leaving just a close.

panelDocSuggestionCard.about: The card under the suggestion being viewed: who proposed it, which one, why, accept or reject.

s1.name: With a reason
s1.note: It gave a why: written on the card, with 'Reject / Accept' below.

s2.name: No reason
s2.note: No why given: only who proposed it and which one.

panelDocReviewStrip.about: The strip above the body when 'View changes' opens the doc: how many of the AI teammate's changes are left, previous/next, collapse.

s1.name: Some left
s1.note: '3 changes by Cheese', with previous/next and collapse.

s2.name: All reverted
s2.note: All spots reverted: becomes 'All reverted', collapsing to just the collapse control.

panelDocReviewCard.about: The card under the change being viewed: which one; revert it if unwanted.

s1.name: Viewing which change
s1.note: '1/3' plus a 'Revert this' button; the button is disabled while busy.

panelDocThreadCard.about: One card per comment thread: the quoted characters on top, each reply below; while the AI teammate is answering it says which step it's on. Only the thread being viewed gets the reply box and resolve.

s1.name: Viewing a thread
s1.note: Viewing this thread: the reply box and 'Resolve' open below.

s2.name: Cheese is answering
s2.note: Not viewing this thread: it's editing the doc, the card says which step it's on, offers 'Stop'.

s3.name: Resolved
s3.note: A resolved thread: viewing it offers 'Reopen', with no reply box.

s4.name: Unknown whether the write landed
s4.note: The last write's result is unknown: it says so and offers 'Resend'.

panelDocComments.about: The content of the comment column: the composer and the threads — unresolved and resolved viewed separately, one card per thread, the conversation laid out.

s1.name: Unresolved
s1.note: Viewing the unresolved ones: a thread started by a person, Cheese replied once.

s2.name: Viewing resolved
s2.note: Switched to 'Resolved': only the handled thread remains.

s3.name: None at all
s3.note: No comments on this doc yet: an empty-state line, not blank.

panelDocCommentPanel.about: The comment column: docked to the right of the body when wide enough, over the body when narrow; the width is draggable. Holds DocComments — open, locate and close are driven from outside.

s1.name: The body cell
s1.note: The panel manages docking, the drawer and its width itself; normally it's a column to the right of the body holding the body (the slot below) and the comments. This shows the body in the slot.

panelDocSurface.about: The document body itself: takes a real collaborative document, draws it with tiptap, wrapped in this set of blocks, overlays and collaborative cursors. The top bar and comment column are someone else's concern.

s1.name: Open a doc
s1.note: This one is titled 'Rollout process': the body is drawn block by block; '/' at a line start inserts a block, and the selection toolbar has AI teammate and comment.

s2.name: Still loading
s2.note: The body is still on its way: draws a skeleton, the editor gives way.

panelDocProse.about: The prose column itself: mounts an editor that already exists and lays the whole typography set over it — heading sizes, paragraph spacing, lists, tables, code blocks, quotes, comment marks, edit marks and collaborative cursors. Locating paragraphs and flashing a passage are someone else's concern.

s1.name: An article
s1.note: Handed an editor holding 'Rollout process': headings a size up, a little air between paragraphs, the body laid out as a column capped at 720px.

s2.name: Empty doc
s2.note: The editor is empty: the ghost placeholder line shows up in the body, the caret resting at its left edge.

s3.name: Keyboard focus
s3.note: Focus arrived in the body by keyboard: a focus ring is drawn around the editor box.

previewPanelHeadBar.about: Preview top bar: 'Publish site' on the left (a project-level action, jumping to the website block on the project overview) and open-in-new-tab, fullscreen and reload on the right — every one of them acts on the current preview.

s1.name: Looking at the current preview
s1.note: The first control on the right opens it in a new tab; with a web page or an image there is also fullscreen, and reload at the far right.

s2.name: The image, fullscreen
s2.note: Images get fullscreen too (they are only accurate when enlarged, and wheel zoom is only live in fullscreen); once it is fullscreen that control turns into exit fullscreen.

previewPanelFrameStage.about: The web/app tier: a little browser row (back, forward, reload, address bar, the platform › tunnel › app chain) over a layer of frames; when the app sleeps, a static snapshot and a wake card cover it, and a region can still be picked on the page.

s1.name: A running app
s1.note: The address bar shows where this frame is now and all three links of the chain are green; resource, instance and readiness are inside the chain's details.

s2.name: Two frames both running
s2.note: The frame on stage takes the reader's input, the other is kept without being re-mounted: hidden away, taking no input; the pane that names a file also gets open and download.

s3.name: The new content did not land
s3.note: What is on screen is still the previous page: say which step failed and offer a retry.

s4.name: Picking a region on an app
s4.note: While picking is on, a transparent overlay covers the app; drag out a rectangle.

s5.name: The app is asleep
s5.note: The teammate's computer sleeps: the platform link stays green, the tunnel and app links turn amber (waiting), the page becomes the last static snapshot, dimmed, with a card offering to wake and restart the app.

s6.name: Waking
s6.note: After pressing wake the card becomes steps — start the computer, connect the tunnel, the teammate restarts the app, wait for the port — each ticked in turn; the ones after the current step stay empty.

previewPanelDocStage.about: The document stage: a document bar (name, type, edit, history, the other reading, download) plus the body. Word, slides, sheets and Markdown all come through here.

s1.name: A Markdown file
s1.note: Markdown is not converted to PDF: it is shown as what it is, read by the same renderer the chat uses.

s2.name: This deployment has no converter
s2.note: Same for any file: say plainly that document preview is off rather than offering a viewer that cannot render.

s3.name: Refresh failed, the previous version is still up
s3.note: What is on screen is not the latest: the bar says so and names the error; the body stays readable.

s4.name: The other reading: web view
s4.note: A second way to read the same document: the elements carry addressable ids, a sheet cell's address among them, and those ids are the ones used to change the file.

previewPanelImageStage.about: The image stage: an image laid into the pane, where a region can be circled and a sentence written, and the composited image handed to the room.

s1.name: An image
s1.note: The image fills the stage, with 'open in new window' in the corner for the original file; circling and annotating happen right on it.

s2.name: The bytes are not here yet
s2.note: Nothing to draw yet: a spinner, not a blank block.

s3.name: The annotation would not composite
s3.note: Circled and written, but the composited image was not produced: the image stays, and the line below names the error.

previewPanelPage.about: Web preview: hands the server-rendered page to a sandboxed iframe (allow-scripts only, not same-origin); changing the page swaps the srcdoc.

s1.name: A web page
s1.note: Server-rendered html handed to a frame: it inherits the parent's CSP, so scripts run but the network is shut off by the page's own CSP.

previewPanelMarkdown.about: Markdown reading view: rendered the way documents are read (blocks, diagrams and formulas like in a doc), and lets the reader point at a sentence to quote it.

s1.name: A markdown snippet
s1.note: A single newline in the file is a soft break; links open a new page.

s2.name: A commented file
s2.note: The words a comment is about carry a mark; the thread being read is drawn stronger.

previewPanelSlides.about: Slide reader: a toolbar on top (thumbnails, previous/next, jump, fit page, present, download), the current slide in the middle.

s1.name: No slides yet
s1.note: Bytes still on their way or not there yet: an empty-state line.

s2.name: Can't convert
s2.note: This PDF won't convert to slides: says 'Preview unavailable for now; you can download the original'.

previewPanelPages.about: Paged view: draws a PDF page by page, only when scrolled into view; click to 'point at a spot', select text to quote.

s1.name: Waiting to point
s1.note: The toolbar has the 'Point at a spot' button; this file has no verified version, so it can say 'Verify the version first' but stays disabled.

previewPanelSheet.about: Spreadsheet preview: CSV/TSV and workbooks laid out as a table with headers, and a toggle to view the raw text.

s1.name: A CSV
s1.note: Comma-separated text laid out as a table, first row as header.

previewPanelThumbRail.about: The thumbnail column beside the slides: one per page, click to jump; a page is drawn only when scrolled into view.

s1.name: A stack of thumbnails
s1.note: Five pages, on page 1: a button per page with the page number below.

previewPanelLocator.about: The bar that appears after 'point at a spot': write a line, then decide whether it becomes a comment on that spot or goes into the conversation for a teammate.

s1.name: Pointed at a spot
s1.note: On top, what it points at (label + that sentence); below, an input and two exits: comment / send.

s2.name: This file takes no comments
s2.note: A library original or a message attachment takes no comments, so only 'send' is offered.

previewPanelPickToggle.about: The 'Select region' toggle on the preview bar: only offered on web preview; press it to drag out a region on the page.

s1.name: On
s1.note: Lit while on (given an icon, the word is in the title); press again to turn off.

s2.name: Off
s2.note: Off is the default look.

previewPanelRegionPick.about: Region select for the app tier: the app has no bridge to read the DOM, so a transparent mask is laid over the iframe and the reader drags out a rectangle.

s1.name: Laid over the page
s1.note: Normally an invisible transparent mask: press, drag, release; the dragged region is sent up with its geometry and the viewport at the time. Too small a gesture (usually a click) is not reported.

previewPanelViewportToolbar.about: The design-preview viewport tools: pick desktop/tablet/mobile, zoom out/in, show the scale, fit to viewport.

s1.name: Desktop
s1.note: Desktop selected, scale 100%.

s2.name: Zoomed halfway
s2.note: Scale 50%: the number follows.

previewPanelRedactSwatch.about: The small preview of a redaction style (the toolbar's row): solid black, 3x3 mosaic, 7x7 noise — the grey cells come from a fixed formula, identical on every render.

s1.name: Solid
s1.note: A single black block.

s2.name: Mosaic
s2.note: A 3x3 grid of grey cells.

s3.name: Noise
s3.note: A 7x7 grid of grey cells.

previewPanelSketchToolbar.about: The annotation tool row on an image: select region, pen/line/arrow/rectangle/ellipse/text/redact, colour, undo-redo-clear, write what to change, add to the thread.

s1.name: Pen
s1.note: Pen selected: the colour wheel is shown; when there are strokes, 'Write what to change' and 'Add to thread' appear on the right.

s2.name: Redact
s2.note: Redact tool selected (or a redaction is selected): the colour wheel becomes the redaction-style row.

previewPanelSketchOverlay.about: Draws the annotations already on the screen onto one SVG layer (handles on the selected/edited one): pen, line, arrow, rectangle, ellipse, text, redact.

s1.name: A few strokes
s1.note: A freehand stroke and a rectangle annotation, laid back onto the image to scale.

previewPanelRegionNote.about: The small card that appears when pointing at a region of an image: it says what it points at, then write what to change, send or cancel.

s1.name: Pointing at this region
s1.note: On top, what it points at (label + that sentence); below, the input and 'Send'. It says so when the region is outside the view.

previewPanelDesignImage.about: Design preview: an image laid into the viewport, zoomable, pannable, region-selectable, annotation layer toggleable; scale and 'Fit to viewport' on top.

s1.name: An image
s1.note: Zoom, scale and 'Fit to viewport' on top; the image below, wheel-zoomable and space-pannable.

previewPanelRevisionList.about: A document's revision list: several pending (replace/add/remove), accept or reject one by one, or handle all at once; read-only versions offer no handling.

s1.name: Three revisions
s1.note: '3 revisions' on top; each row below says which paragraph and how it changes.

previewPanelRoomFileHistory.about: A file's save history in a channel: every save keeps a version, any version can be downloaded or restored, the current one is marked.

s1.name: Several saves
s1.note: The newest is marked 'current'; each version says which one, who saved it and from which source.

previewPanelRoomFileEditor.about: Editing a channel file in the browser: the top bar has the file name, read-only/unsaved/versions saved, and save history and close on the right; the editor is embedded below.

s1.name: This one can't be edited here
s1.note: No session, with the reason 'This kind of file can't be edited in the browser': it says so instead of showing an editor that won't open.

manageDeniedView.about: The screen a member sees when they click space management and the guard blocks them: it says 'You don't have management permission', and the way out goes back to the task list, not out of the space.

s1.name: Blocked from the management area
s1.note: Same shape as the project's 'No access' (the same AccessNotice), only the words belong to this board; the exit goes back to the task list — the person is usually still a member here.

publishTaskView.about: Publish page: the publish form on the left, saved as a draft as it is written; the header's Drafts lists my drafts in this space. Cheese is the app's one panel, docked on the right when this page opens on desktop. While it writes this draft, the app's Cheese host draws a named pointer on the form that follows what it fills in; this component does not draw it.

s1.name: Writing a draft
s1.note: Default cell: the form, with 'Drafts 3' and 'Draft saved' in the header, and 'Needs admin review after publishing' beside the publish button.

s3.name: Space not ready
s3.note: Categories and domain groups are still on their way: no form, and the publish button is disabled.

s4.name: Several tasks from one file
s4.note: Above the form, the tasks Cheese made from one file: the first is published, the second shows 1 missing after Publish all, the third is being filled in. Publish all (2) sits at the end.

s5.name: Cheese closed
s5.note: With the panel closed, the header has a button that brings it back; while it is open the button is gone.

s6.name: Publish refused
s6.note: Publish was clicked and the server refused it: beside the publish button, the server's own words (in red) replace the review note and stay until the next publish or another draft opens.

s7.name: Publish all with one refused
s7.note: After "Publish all", the server refused the second task: the note says how many went out, and the refused one carries the server's own words.

basicInfoView.about: Space settings 'Basic info': avatar, name, intro, plus a 'Max visible tasks' row for admins and a danger zone (delete space) for owners. Reads and writes are in the container; here it only draws and emits.

s1.name: Owner and admin
s1.note: Default cell: the form holds this board's name and intro, an admin sees 'Max visible tasks', and a danger zone visible only to the creator is added at the bottom.

s2.name: Just a regular member
s2.note: Neither admin nor owner: the max row and the danger zone are not drawn — showing a button that is bound to fail (403) is worse than showing none.

spaceSettingsIndexView.about: The shell around space settings: on desktop the grey left side is the list (whose settings these are), the white right side is this section; on phones it's full screen, list first then a section. This layer has its own URL, each item a route.

s1.name: Basic info selected
s1.note: Default cell: the left list shows the seven sections of space settings (currently 'Basic info'), this item is highlighted, and the right side holds its content.

s2.name: No section selected yet
s2.note: 'active' empty means no section selected yet: on narrow screens this is 'stopped at the list' (full-screen list, tap an item to enter). This catalog viewport is desktop width, so you see the desktop shell with no list item highlighted.

spaceGuidanceView.about: Space settings 'AI teammate guidance': a line of explanation, the approach, additional requirements, materials it may read, and save. All empty means this board sets nothing; only each task's own counts.

s1.name: This board set defaults
s1.note: Set: 'Guide with questions' is picked and requirements are written.

s2.name: No defaults yet
s2.note: All six empty means 'nothing said': the materials list also failed to load this time, but failing to load isn't the same as gone, so it isn't treated as invalid — that field becomes an explanatory line, offering no candidates.

briefView.about: Task detail 'Brief' tab: the task brief (rich text) and the materials list; whether it's clickable and how many times it's downloadable is said by the server. The section isn't drawn when there are no materials.

s1.name: Brief and materials
s1.note: Default cell: the task brief on top, a 'Materials' section below listing two downloadable files.

s2.name: Brief only, no materials
s2.note: This task brings no materials: the whole materials section isn't drawn, no empty heading left — just the brief section.

s3.name: Rubric kept to graders
s3.note: The publisher or a space admin still sees the rubric, marked as visible to graders only; students do not see this section.

insightsView.about: Task detail 'Data' tab: how many claimed this task, how far they got, where they stalled, when they moved. Every number is computed from the roster and submissions.

s1.name: Claimed and submitted
s1.note: Default cell: four KPIs (participants / submitted / pass rate / idle since starting), a participation trend, how far they got, squad makeup.

s2.name: Read failure, not drawn as 0
s2.note: Neither roster nor submissions loaded: it explains the failure and offers retry, instead of drawing a '0 claimed, 0% pass' board pretending all is well.

s3.name: Neither author nor admin
s3.note: Those without access are told why, instead of seeing an empty table.

s4.name: Task not found
s4.note: The task itself didn't load: says 'Task not found', doesn't draw a screen of empty charts.

rosterView.about: Task detail 'Participants' tab: handling applications, viewing submissions per version, filtering by status — all in this one table. Fetching is in the container; here it only reports 'what to do to whom'.

s1.name: Roster loaded
s1.note: Default cell: status-filter tabs on top, a table below — who claimed, when, how far they got, the latest version, the deadline; at the row's end, what that row can do.

s2.name: Roster still loading
s2.note: Not loaded yet: says 'Loading' in place, doesn't say 'No participants' first.

s3.name: Not for you
s3.note: The server gates by permission; 403 is 'not showing you': it spells out that only the author and space admins can see participants.

s4.name: Failed this time
s4.note: Separate from 'not for you': a read failure gives the failure and a retry, not the permission line.

s5.name: No one has claimed
s5.note: Loaded and the roster is indeed empty: only then does it say 'No participants'.

views404.about: The screen someone sees at a nonexistent address: a 'Page not found' line and a button home, catching every path not written out.

s1.name: Page not found
s1.note: What the catch-all at the end of the route table draws: the title is 404, a 'Page not found' line, and the action goes home.

docsSignInView.about: The sign-in page the platform uses for the docs site: while handing the reader over it's a spinning progress ring; on error it spells out the reason and offers a retry.

s1.name: Opening the docs
s1.note: No error yet: not a blank block but a spinning progress ring, with an aria-label saying what it's doing.

s2.name: Won't open, offers a retry
s2.note: On error it becomes a red notice spelling out the reason as-is, with a button below to try again (it shows a spinner while retrying).

addEmailView.about: The screen for adding an email to an account: first fill in the address and self-check against the rules, then it becomes the enter-code step in place once the code is sent.

s1.name: Enter address
s1.note: Step one: the address field carries a 'School or work email recommended' hint, a send button below, and sign-out in the corner.

s2.name: Address taken
s2.note: When this email is already bound to another account, the reason is written on the top line, the form stays, change it and resend.

s3.name: After the code is sent
s3.note: Same screen switches to the code step: says which address the code went to, six boxes, and resending once the one-minute cooldown passes.

appSignInFinishView.about: In the desktop app, waiting for the browser sign-in to be exchanged for its own: success is a signing-in line; failure says this sign-in has expired and offers a button back to sign-in.

s1.name: Exchanging for the app sign-in
s1.note: The link brought back this app-initiated sign-in: the title says 'Signing in', a line below shows it's making progress.

s2.name: This sign-in expired
s2.note: When the link doesn't bring back the app-initiated sign-in: the title says 'Sign-in failed', the reason is in the notice, with a primary button back to sign-in.

appSignInStartView.about: The moment the browser lands the desktop app's sign-in: nothing's decided yet, and the only thing drawable is a progress line showing it's working.

s1.name: Just running
s1.note: There's not a single line of text on this screen: a two-pixel progress line is all there is; the container swaps it out once it has the destination.

backToAppView.about: The screen that hands the sign-in back to the app after the browser flow finishes: says which account it's signing in, hand it over on press, open the app once the app link arrives, and spell out the reason if it can't be handed over.

s1.name: Waiting for the link
s1.note: Nothing settled yet: a progress line, nothing else to press.

s2.name: Ask, then hand over
s2.note: The account to hand over is set: the title says who it signs in, a 'Continue' below hands it over, with switch-account and cancel beside it.

s3.name: App link received
s3.note: After handing over, the app gave its own link: an 'Open Cheese' button here opens the app.

s4.name: Can't hand over
s4.note: The hand-over failed: the title says 'Sign-in failed', the reason is in the notice, telling the person to sign in again in the app.

desktopSignInView.about: The common starting point for sign-in, sign-up and password recovery on the desktop app: a button that opens the browser, and after it's been opened you can open it again or copy the link out.

s1.name: Browser not opened yet
s1.note: Default cell: it explains sign-in happens in the browser, the primary button says 'Sign in in the browser', and 'No account yet?' is below.

s2.name: Opened once
s2.note: The browser has opened once: an 'Opened; you'll return here when done' line is added, the button becomes 'Open the browser again', plus a copy-link button.

s3.name: Can't open the browser
s3.note: If the browser won't launch, the reason is on the top line and the button stays put to try again.

s4.name: The sign-up cell
s4.note: Same shell, a different entry: the title goes from 'Sign in to Cheese' to 'Sign up for Cheese', and the line below from 'No account yet' to 'Already have an account'.

oAuthCompleteView.about: The screen after a third-party account comes back verified: a line while loading; once loaded, choose between 'Create a new account' and 'Link an existing account', each with its own form; when the state can't be fetched it says so and offers the way back to sign-in.

s1.name: Still reading the returned state
s1.note: Identity not in hand yet (or still being checked): a progress line, nothing else drawn.

s2.name: Create a new account
s2.note: State in hand: the title greets the name in the identity, defaulting to 'Create a new account' — username, nickname and email fields, with the consent checkbox below.

s3.name: This site needs an invite code
s3.note: An extra field when sign-up needs an invite code: like the sign-up page, submitting empty is stopped by the self-check.

s4.name: State unavailable
s4.note: The third-party state didn't come back (expired or errored): the title says 'Can't continue signing in', the reason is in the lead, with a primary button back to sign-in.

oAuthErrorView.about: The screen after a third-party sign-in fails: the title states the result; when the error code carries a reason it's spelled out on its own line, and you go back to sign-in or retry at the provider.

s1.name: Result only
s1.note: The error code carried nothing else: the title 'Sign-in failed' suffices, with just a primary button back to sign-in below.

s2.name: With a reason
s2.note: When the error code translates to a sentence it gets its own line: the reason is in the notice, no longer repeating the title.

s3.name: Can retry at the provider
s3.note: When the address carries a provider, a secondary button is added: it reads 'Sign in again with <provider>' using the provider's name, and jumps right back.

oAuthSuccessView.about: The wrapping-up screen after a third-party sign-in returns: while reading the session it says which provider it's completing; once read it says sign-in succeeded and is redirecting; on error it spells out the reason and offers the way back to sign-in.

s1.name: Completing third-party sign-in
s1.note: Still exchanging the cookie from the redirect for a session: the title says 'Signing in', the lead names the provider, a progress line below.

s2.name: Signed in, redirecting
s2.note: The session is exchanged: the title goes from 'Signing in' to 'Signed in', the lead says 'Redirecting', waiting to be taken where it belongs.

s3.name: Exchange failed
s3.note: Holding the cookie but no session: the title says 'Sign-in failed', the reason is in the notice, with a primary button back to sign-in.

oAuthVerifyView.about: Asking for the password once when linking a third-party account to an existing one: says which email is being linked; a wrong password can be written on the field, or on its own line above.

s1.name: Ask for the password once
s1.note: Default cell: the title says 'Link account', the lead names the email, a password field, a 'Verify and link' button, sign-in below.

s2.name: Wrong password, on the field
s2.note: A wrong password alone doesn't redden the whole page: that line lands under the password field itself, fixing it in place.

s3.name: General failure
s3.note: When it isn't the password (say the address is taken) it gets its own line: the reason above the form, the field still clean.

passkeyOfferView.about: After sign-in, encouraging adding a passkey: accept and not-now are the same size, and an account that declined can quietly say 'Don't ask again'.

s1.name: Encourage adding one
s1.note: Default cell: it explains signing in with fingerprint/face on this device, two equal-sized buttons — add, and not now.

s2.name: Declined before, can stop the prompt
s2.note: This person declined before: a quiet 'Don't ask again' is added; clicking it stops the asking, clearly not being pushed.

s3.name: Something went wrong adding
s3.note: When this device can't create a passkey, the reason is on the top line, both buttons still there.

signInView.about: The sign-in page: notice or error, the ways in (the last used one first with a small tag), and the username/password form.

s1.name: Default order: one-click ways first
s1.note: This browser has no sign-in history: the one-click ways come first, then 'or', then the password form; the title line carries a link to sign up.

s2.name: Last used a passkey
s2.note: With sign-in history, that way is drawn first and tagged 'Last used'; the container orders it first too.

s3.name: An attempt rejected
s3.note: When the username or password is wrong the reason is on the top line; during the wait the form's button is held, until enough seconds pass.

s4.name: Returning with a notice
s4.note: A notice travels as its own green message: e.g. just reset the password, or just signed out; it says a line before letting you fill the form.

verify2FaView.about: The two-step-verification step: the trust-this-device checkbox, the input for the current code type, a link back to sign-in, and the dialog urging a fresh set of backup codes after one is used.

s1.name: Enter the authenticator code
s1.note: Default cell: the lead says to take a 6-digit code from your authenticator app, the checkbox guards 'don't ask this device for 30 days', and below is how long repeated failures lock you out.

s2.name: Switch to a backup code
s2.note: Switching to a backup code changes only what to fill and the button: the lead becomes 'Enter an 8-digit backup code', the button reads 'Verify backup code'.

s3.name: Wrong code
s3.note: When the code is wrong the reason is on the top line, the field stays put to refill.

s4.name: The prompt after using a backup code
s4.note: Passing this step with a backup code pops a dialog in place: it spells out that each backup code works once, urging you to generate a new set now (not opened here, only drawn).

requestView.about: The first step of signing in with an email code: fill in the address, self-check against the rules, send, and the way back to sign-in.

s1.name: Enter address
s1.note: Default cell: the title says 'Sign in with an email code', an email field, a 'Send code' button, sign-in below.

s2.name: Sending too often
s2.note: Sending repeatedly within a minute is blocked by the server: the reason is on the top line, press the button again once enough time passes.

emailCodeVerifyView.about: The second step of signing in with an email code: says which address the code went to, six boxes, a one-minute resend countdown and the way back to sign-in.

s1.name: Enter code
s1.note: Default cell: the title says 'Enter the code', the lead names the address the code went to, six boxes, submitting allowed once filled.

s2.name: Resend countdown
s2.note: Just after sending, the 'Resend' control is tucked away, replaced by a countdown of how many seconds remain; it returns when the seconds run out.

s3.name: Wrong code
s3.note: When the code is wrong or expired the reason is on the top line, the boxes cleared to re-enter.

passwordStartView.about: The first step of password recovery: fill in the registered email to send a reset link; once sent, the screen becomes a 'Check your email' line in place.

s1.name: Enter registered email
s1.note: Default cell: it explains a reset link will be sent to this email, a 'Send reset email' button, 'Remembered it?' and sign-in below.

s2.name: Email sent
s2.note: After sending, the form gives way to the result: the title becomes 'Check your email', a 'Reset-password email sent' line, leaving just a button back to sign-in.

s3.name: Can't send
s3.note: When sending fails the reason is on the top line, the form stays, change the address or try later.

passwordVerifyView.about: The second step opened by the reset link: enter the new password twice, with the account name hidden in the form for password managers, mismatches written on the field in place.

s1.name: Set a new password
s1.note: Default cell: the title says 'Set a new password', new-password and confirm fields, with a hint of at least 8 characters including letters, digits and symbols.

s2.name: Link expired
s2.note: When the reset token is expired the reason is on the top line: sends you back to sign-in to redo password recovery.

signupStartView.about: The create-account screen: username, nickname, email and password in two groups, each self-checked; an extra field when an invite code is needed, and the consent checkbox below.

s1.name: Fill the form
s1.note: Default cell: title 'Create account', five fields each with its own rules, the consent checkbox below; the primary button lights only once the config is complete.

s2.name: This site needs an invite code
s2.note: An extra field when sign-up needs an invite code: like the others it self-checks; submitting empty is stopped.

s3.name: Sign-up failed
s3.note: When the backend refuses (username taken, duplicate email) the reason goes on the top line, the form's contents stay, fix one field and resubmit.

s4.name: Consent not loaded
s4.note: When the consent versions didn't come back, a line under the consent field gives the reason it couldn't, and the primary button stays held as the config is incomplete.

verifyEmailView.about: The verify-email screen after sign-up: six boxes, ask for the password once more if a refresh dropped it, ask for consent again if it wasn't kept, and a resend countdown below.

s1.name: Enter code
s1.note: Default cell: title 'Verify email', the lead names the address the code went to, six boxes, with resend and sign-in below.

s2.name: Refresh dropped the password, ask again
s2.note: A refresh lost the half-finished sign-up state: an extra password field, spelling out 'Enter the password you set at sign-up', so verification doesn't succeed with no usable password.

s3.name: Resend countdown
s3.note: Just after sending, 'Resend' is tucked away, replaced by a countdown of how many seconds remain.

s4.name: Verification failed
s4.note: When the code is wrong or expired the reason is on the top line, the boxes cleared to start over.

adminCreditsPageView.about: The plans-and-credits page: plans on top, teams below (with plan/type filters and search); opening a team, creating a plan and granting credits all pop up as overlays.

s1.name: Plans and teams both loaded
s1.note: Default cell: the plans table on top, the teams table below, both drawing real data — a personal team shows the owner's nickname in the team column, a shared team shows the member count.

s2.name: First load
s2.note: Neither has arrived: each table draws its own skeleton, same shape as loaded, no reflow.

s3.name: Teams table failed
s3.note: The teams path failing doesn't drag down the plans path: only the teams block becomes 'failed + message + retry', the plans table still draws.

s4.name: Opened a team
s4.note: Clicking a team row slides out a panel on the right (full screen on phones): plan, each credit grant, operation log; granting credits is a button.

s5.name: New plan
s5.note: The dialog the 'New plan' button pops up: name, applies to, credits and limit, available models all empty awaiting input.

adminRunRecordsPageView.about: The run-records screen: errors the platform hit across projects and the things it handled itself, one kind per row; opening a row shows that kind's most recent full text on the right and which projects and threads it appeared in.

s1.name: One kind per row
s1.note: Default cell: errors first, self-handled after; three KPIs in the header say how many error kinds, how many times in all, how many the platform handled itself.

s2.name: First load
s2.note: Overview not yet in hand: three KPIs draw skeletons; the table header is already up, but there are no data rows yet.

s3.name: Read failure doesn't say 'none'
s3.note: A dead endpoint should stay put: it explains the failure and offers retry, rather than drawing 'No run records' — that hides a failure as an absence.

s4.name: No records for now
s4.note: Loaded and the window truly has none: only then does it say 'No run records'.

s5.name: Open a kind for its detail
s5.note: Clicking a row slides out detail on the right: the most recent full text, which project threads it appeared in (clickable) and the stack trace.

legalDocumentView.about: A published terms-of-service or privacy policy: version, effective date and its own body; the body is fetched by the container and handed over, it fetches not a single byte itself.

s1.name: A policy
s1.note: Default cell: the version and effective date on top, the body rendered from Markdown below.

s2.name: Unreadable
s2.note: When this version isn't fetched, a reason line replaces the body, not a blank page.

adminStatsPageView.about: The admin stats page: one shell (header + window switcher) drawing whichever screen this category is — platform, performance, delivery pipeline, usage, product, feedback trend, integrations status. On a whole-block read failure the header stays and the body becomes the failure.

s1.name: The platform screen
s1.note: Default category: account stock and additions, machine ledger, three health tiles. Those machine rows are a stock, not an online count, and that line is on screen.

s2.name: The delivery pipeline screen
s2.note: A different kind draws a different screen: five cards, four live stages on a rail, 'waiting on you / stuck' and failure codes. The four stages are throughput at different moments, not a funnel.

s3.name: The usage screen
s3.note: Tokens and calls in the window, the biggest-spending project, cost, and the quota-exhausted list. 'Unpriced tokens' are counted separately, not folded into the total to look free.

s4.name: The product screen
s4.note: North star, how far hand-offs got. The two that can't be computed are drawn with a reason (no data source), not a fake 0.

s5.name: The feedback trend screen
s5.note: Four counts, a status distribution, three lines, and on the right a 'needs attention' ten rows — that block goes through another request, and only it is a skeleton while the list hasn't arrived.

s6.name: The performance screen
s6.note: The only screen reading process memory: endpoint latencies at this moment, the slowest one right now, the route table. 'Slowest right now' gives the conclusion outright, not making you find it in the table.

s7.name: First load
s7.note: This category hasn't arrived: the header stays (it's the page's name, not data), and each body block draws its own skeleton.

s8.name: Whole-block read failure
s8.note: Nothing came in for this category and there's a server line: the whole body becomes the read failure — the header's still there, the line is copied as-is, retry is the only primary action.

settingsGeneralView.about: Account settings 'General': the desktop app's own settings on this computer, appearing only in the app. The header first explains these settings apply only to this computer, and below there's just one row — launch at login.

s1.name: Launch at login
s1.note: The only row: 'Launch at login' and a line of explanation on the left, a switch on the right (it asks the system when the page opens; until answered it's held).

notificationsView.about: Account settings 'Notifications': three blocks top to bottom — channels (in-app / push / email), do-not-disturb (quiet hours / digest frequency), and an eight-events by three-channels matrix. Toggling saves; the result shows at the header's top-right.

s1.name: Notification prefs loaded
s1.note: All three blocks: two cards side by side, the eight-row, three-column matrix below, each cell a dot.

s2.name: First load
s2.note: Prefs not loaded yet: a spinner in one card's spot, nothing else drawn (so 'not loaded yet' isn't drawn as 'all off').

s3.name: Read failure
s3.note: On failure it writes the real reason in place and offers a retry — not a spread of 'all off'.

s4.name: Saving one matrix cell
s4.note: After toggling one matrix cell only that cell goes busy: it's held in place, everything else's display stays put — greying the whole page reads as 'the whole page is saving'.

s5.name: Saving a channel switch
s5.note: After toggling the 'in-app' switch, only that spot goes busy: the switch holds and spins itself, nothing else moves.

profileView.about: Account settings 'Profile': avatar, nickname, username, intro in four rows, and a save bar that appears only once something changed. Nickname and intro are this page's own draft, submitted once made dirty.

s1.name: Profile in hand
s1.note: Default cell: a link back to your own page at the header's right; four rows below — avatar, nickname, username, intro.

s2.name: Person not loaded
s2.note: When the container hasn't got the account, the whole page is just a header — the form and the link back are drawn only once the person arrives.

s3.name: Saving
s3.note: After submitting, the save bar surfaces, the receipt on its right reading 'Saving...'.

s4.name: Saved
s4.note: Saved: the receipt becomes a green 'Saved', fading out on its own after a few seconds.

s5.name: Can't save
s5.note: When the server refuses it copies the reason; the receipt is a red line (a reason is appended after 'Save failed').

realNameView.about: Account settings 'Real-name info': once filled it shows only masked name and student ID (a separate confirm to see the full ones); when unfilled, a button to fill it in, and below, the access log of who viewed this record.

s1.name: Not loaded yet
s1.note: The record hasn't come back: a fixed-height card holds the spot so the page doesn't jump the moment it loads.

s2.name: Read failure
s2.note: When the record can't be loaded, the card writes a reason line (it no longer counts as 'loading' then).

s3.name: Never filled in
s3.note: Read back 'no such record': it says it's not filled yet and offers a button to fill it in.

s4.name: Fill it the first time
s4.note: Opening the form, name and student ID are required, the rest optional; two buttons below — cancel and save.

s5.name: Already filled in
s5.note: With a record, only the masked values are shown row by row, with 'Show full info' and 'Edit' buttons at the top-right.

s6.name: Your own views
s6.note: After filling, an access log is added below: this shows the two entries where you viewed it yourself — the mark, a 'You viewed the full info' line, which space, and when. (The 'someone else viewed it' rows need the outer scope and can't be mounted standalone in the catalog; see the note in the fixtures.)

securityView.about: Account settings 'Password & security': three blocks by 'how you get in' — sign-in methods (password, passkey, two-step verification), linked accounts, browsers and apps signed in; changing the password and enabling two-step verification are both in dialogs.

s1.name: All three lists present
s1.note: Default cell: a passkey (it takes its own detail row), two-step verification off, one linked account, two signed-in browsers.

s2.name: Browser doesn't support passkeys
s2.note: When this browser can't create a passkey, that row says why and the 'Add' button is held.

s3.name: Two-step verification on
s3.note: With two-step verification on, a lit dot precedes the status row and a 'Backup codes' block is added below.

s4.name: No linked accounts
s4.note: The linked-accounts block reads empty: it writes 'No linked accounts' in place, not an empty row.

s5.name: No other sign-ins
s5.note: The sign-in list reads empty: that block writes 'No other sign-ins' in place, and the top-right 'Sign out other devices' doesn't appear (no other devices to sign out).

s6.name: Change-password dialog
s6.note: The dialog popped by 'Edit': new-password and confirm fields, a mismatch written on the field in place.

s7.name: Enable two-step: scan
s7.note: The first of three steps: a 'Scan the QR code with your authenticator app' line, the QR code, and the secret to enter by hand when scanning isn't possible.

s8.name: Enable two-step: enter code
s8.note: The second step: type the 6 digits from the authenticator into a row of boxes, verification allowed once filled.

s9.name: Enable two-step: backup codes
s9.note: The third step: list this set of backup codes, remind that they're shown only this once and each works once, and offer a button to copy the whole set.

s10.name: Closing refused: still a team's only owner
s10.note: The server refuses the close: this person is still the only owner of a team that others are in, or that someone can still enter through a pending invitation or joining without approval. The reason stays in the dialog, names the team, and says to transfer ownership, or cancel the invitations and turn on join approval, first.

modelConnectionsView.about: Team Models lists platform models, device logins, and encrypted API keys and model services. Administrators add, recheck, rename and remove connections, and choose their available models.

s1.name: No connections
s1.note: Each connection card shows its own empty state and keeps its add actions.

s2.name: Removing on an offline device
s2.note: Removed while its device is offline: no longer used, and its line is marked as removing; opened, it says it logs out when the device comes online, with no check or remove buttons.

s3.name: A stored key failed its check
s3.note: The service refused the key when it was tested again: its line is marked in red as failing the check; opened, it shows what the service said, and it can still be tested again, renamed or removed.

s4.name: Two logins on one device
s4.note: Two Claude accounts logged in on the workstation: one line each, each opened, checked again, renamed and removed on its own; removing one leaves the other in use.

s5.name: Both kinds of connection
s5.note: Sample data includes device subscriptions, services and API keys, plus platform-held keys and services, one row per connection.

s6.name: Adding my connection
s6.note: Pick one of your existing connections to add to the team; it serves only your own assistant.

channelBrowseView.about: The project's 'All channels': channels I can see in a list (findable, joinable, leavable); project managers can create channels on this page too. The sidebar lists only what I've joined; others are found here.

s1.name: List channels
s1.note: Default cell: a search box, a row of filters (all / joined / archived, each with a count), one row per channel below — name, description, headcount, with 'Join' or 'Leave' on the right.

s2.name: First load
s2.note: No channel loaded yet and still reading: a spinner, not saying 'No channels' first.

s3.name: Read failure
s3.note: When the channel list fails, it writes the reason in place and offers a retry.

s4.name: None visible
s4.note: Loaded but no channel I can see: it says 'No channels' in place.

s5.name: New channel
s5.note: The dialog a manager pops by pressing 'New': name, description, a 'Members only' checkbox; creation allowed once the name is filled.

projectTasksView.about: The project's 'All tasks': tasks grouped by 'whose turn is next' (to-do, in review, in progress, not started), the ones waiting on a person written in warm colour; filterable on top by 'whose', 'which channel' and 'show closed'.

s1.name: Tasks in progress
s1.note: Default cell: a row of filters (all / mine / helping / others, each with a count), a channel menu, show-closed; below, grouped by status, one task per row.

s2.name: First load
s2.note: Tasks not loaded yet and still reading: a spinner; the counts on the filters aren't written yet (a 0 there isn't a real 0).

s3.name: Read failure
s3.note: When the task list fails, it writes the line and offers a retry.

s4.name: Nothing at all
s4.note: Loaded and this filter has nothing: it says 'No tasks' in place.

s5.name: Show closed
s5.note: Switching to 'Closed' stops grouping, everything drops into the 'Closed' group, and the counts come from the server's set.

s6.name: Folds a few stalled
s6.note: Work idle for fourteen days folds into a bottom 'Stalled' section, first saying just 'N stalled', listing them only when opened.

s7.name: Only one channel
s7.note: After picking a channel from the channel menu, that chip lights up and the list keeps only tasks in that channel.

projectOverviewView.about: The page you land on entering a project: the project goals, recent progress (by day), who's doing what (by owner), and what's been made (handed-over artifacts and sites).

s1.name: All four blocks present
s1.note: Default cell: the left column is the project goals (with an 'Edit project goals') and recent progress; the right column is who's doing what and what's been made (those two artifacts).

s2.name: No document yet
s2.note: When the document is empty (not unreadable) it offers a 'No project goals yet' line saying what to write, and a 'Write project goals'.

s3.name: Progress unreadable
s3.note: When recent progress fails, only that block explains the reason and offers a retry, not turning the whole page into one error.

s4.name: No progress in two weeks
s4.note: Loaded, but nothing to say for the last two weeks: it says 'No progress in the last two weeks' in place.

s5.name: Who's-doing-what empty
s5.note: When there's not a single task in progress, that block says 'No tasks in progress'.

s6.name: Challenge-born project with a deadline
s6.note: A project born from a task adds a deadline line above the document: if your own registration was approved it says 'Submission deadline', otherwise 'Task deadline'.

mineView.about: The my-teams page: projects under your own name are not here (a project is not a team); each team you have joined is one row that opens the team page.

s1.name: Two teams
s1.note: Default state: one row per team with avatar, name and a one-line intro; tapping one opens the team page.

s2.name: First load
s2.note: Not back yet: a spinner and a "Loading…" line, not the empty state.

s3.name: Could not load
s3.note: A failed read says so and offers a reload, rather than showing "You haven't joined a team yet".

s4.name: No teams at all
s4.note: Read, and there really are none: only now does it say "You haven't joined a team yet" and offer the next step.

exploreView.about: The find-teams page: a search box on top; before searching it shows the "Recruiting" placeholder, and after searching it swaps in results, no-results or a search failure.

s1.name: Not searched yet
s1.note: Default state: the search box is empty and below it sits the recruiting placeholder (coming soon).

s2.name: Found teams
s2.note: After a keyword is submitted: a list of results, each with avatar, name and a one-line intro.

s3.name: No results
s3.note: Searched, and nothing matched: it says "No teams found" in place, without a retry that cannot help.

s4.name: Search failed
s4.note: This request failed, which is not the same as "no results": the failure is stated in place with a retry kept.

s5.name: No permission
s5.note: 401/403 means "you may not see this", not "this read failed": it says so and offers no retry.

adminIntegrationsPageView.about: The admin "Feishu app" page: an admin fills in the platform App ID / Secret / domain once and members connect with one click. The Secret is write-only and never echoed.

s1.name: Already configured
s1.note: Default state: the status line reads "Configured · App ID · domain" and who last updated it; App ID and domain are filled in, the Secret is always empty.

s2.name: Never configured
s2.note: Never set up: the status line reads "Not configured" and the three fields wait to be filled.

s3.name: Could not load
s3.note: A failed read shows only "could not load" with a retry — no status line and no form, because only a successful read knows whether it is configured.

s4.name: App ID blank
s4.note: Saving with a blank App ID: it says "Enter the App ID first" and the request is never sent.

s5.name: Save failed
s5.note: A rejected save shows the server's own words and leaves every field untouched.

adminSpacesPageView.about: The admin "space applications" page: applications awaiting review, one per row, with approve/reject to the right of the row; rejecting asks for a reason.

s1.name: One of each status
s1.note: Default state: a pending row has approve and reject on its right; approved/rejected rows carry only a status chip and no actions.

s2.name: First load
s2.note: Not back yet: five fixed-height skeleton rows so nothing jumps when data arrives.

s3.name: Could not load
s3.note: A failed read stays in the list's place, states the reason and offers a retry, rather than showing "No applications".

s4.name: None at all
s4.note: Read, and this pile really is empty: only now does it say "No applications.".

s5.name: Reject dialog
s5.note: The dialog opened by "Reject": it names the application, asks for a reason, and keeps "Reject" disabled while the reason is blank.

s6.name: Paging
s6.note: When there is a previous or next page, pager buttons appear at the bottom right; a single page leaves no row of grey buttons.

alertsView.about: The analytics 'alerts' block: the counts of work waiting on someone (tasks to approve, applications to review, stalled tasks…). A count that can be acted on is a button that carries its filter to the tasks block; the rest are plain numbers.

s1.name: Counts with alerts
s1.note: The default: one card per count, and the ones you can act on are buttons that jump to the tasks filtered to them.

s2.name: First load
s2.note: Not back yet: a progress bar, not an empty 'No alerts'.

s3.name: Could not load
s3.note: A failed read states the reason the server gave, with a retry beside it.

s4.name: Nothing waiting
s4.note: Read, and there really is nothing: it says 'No alerts' rather than leaving a blank block.

adminMembersPageView.about: The admin 'members' page: the platform-admin roster in two groups (the root list from config, and the ones added here), with add and remove.

s1.name: The roster
s1.note: The default: two groups, avatars with nickname and handle, account status marks only the exceptions, and remove shows on the added rows only.

s2.name: First load
s2.note: No roster yet: skeleton rows in the table, not a premature empty state.

s3.name: Could not load
s3.note: The table says it could not be read (the server's words as the description) and the retry sits right there.

s4.name: After adding
s4.note: A result notice — a success also speaks, so you can tell which handles were added.

s5.name: Refreshing
s5.note: With a roster already on screen a refresh only dims it (busy); it does not flash the skeleton.

s6.name: Add dialog
s6.note: Search is server-side; candidates already on the roster are drawn disabled, with a badge.

pendingView.about: Requests and invitations: each section owns its loading, failure and results; actions go back to the page.

s1.name: Requests and invitations
s1.note: The three sections show their rows, with cancel, accept or decline for pending items.

s2.name: Loading requests
s2.note: Requests load first; the other two sections retain their original empty states.

s3.name: Loading team invitations
s3.note: Requests have arrived while team invitations are loading.

s4.name: Loading project invitations
s4.note: The team sections have arrived while project invitations are loading.

s5.name: Empty sections
s5.note: All three sections were successfully read and are empty.

s6.name: Requests failed
s6.note: Only requests show a reason and retry; invitations remain usable.

s7.name: Team invitations failed
s7.note: Team invitations retry independently of requests and project invitations.

s8.name: Project invitations failed
s8.note: Project invitations show the failure without hiding the two team sections.

s9.name: Answering a project invitation
s9.note: Only the current project invitation has both buttons disabled; other invitations remain usable.

s10.name: Refreshing with existing rows
s10.note: Each refreshing section retains its existing rows instead of becoming an initial load.

learningView.about: Learning analytics: filter by student and knowledge point, select stuck points or questions, and build a teaching outline.

s1.name: Queues and questions
s1.note: Shows stuck points and questions, with a reason for unavailable review signals.

s2.name: First load
s2.note: Shows progress before queues arrive without prematurely showing empty questions.

s3.name: Load failed
s3.note: A failed queue or question read replaces content with the reason and retry.

s4.name: Empty queues and questions
s4.note: Loaded with no flagged items, stuck points or questions.

s5.name: No member projects
s5.note: No member projects takes precedence even when the queue read failed.

s6.name: Filters and selection
s6.note: Both filters are selected; a question is checked in both its stuck point and list row.

s7.name: Generated outline
s7.note: Shows outline sessions, excerpts and the notice for unavailable questions.

s8.name: Refreshing and building
s8.note: Keeps queues, selections and the outline while the build button is busy.

s9.name: Flagged questions
s9.note: Available review signals show their questions instead of an unavailable reason.

adminMachinesPageView.about: The machines screen: where each MicroCloud host is in its life, which sandboxes are on it, whether the pool has room right now, and how fast sandboxes came up over the last day.

s1.name: One row per host
s1.note: The default: one host in use, one offline, one broken by the provider and given up; opening the one in use shows a working sandbox and one waiting for its host.

s2.name: Not starting new AI teammates
s2.note: The provider broke three hosts within the hour: the page says no new AI teammates are being started, instead of leaving a number to interpret.

s3.name: A failed read is not an empty pool
s3.note: The request failed: say so and offer a retry, rather than drawing an empty pool.

s4.name: An empty pool
s4.note: Read, and there really is no host: only then does it say so.

teamDetailView.about: The team page's rendering half: someone who has not joined sees the team's public side, a member sees the workspace shell - header, parent link, and the middle column left to a child route. Which team to read, whether this person is a member, and how a failure differs from a denial all live in the container `teams/Detail.vue`.

s1.name: A member in the workspace
s1.note: Read, and this person is a member: the workspace shell - header, parent link (the team name), the team intro beside the title, the middle cell left to a child route (empty in the catalog), and no public-facing profile card.

s2.name: Not joined yet: the team's public side
s2.note: The same team, but not a member: the public side - intro, owner, member count - with "Join team" or "Apply to join" below, depending on whether approval is on; no workspace.

s3.name: No team at this address
s3.note: 404: it says no team is at this address, which is not "this read failed", and offers no retry.

s4.name: This read failed
s4.note: A network or server error: this cell says the read failed, with the real reason and a retry.

s5.name: No permission
s5.note: 401/403 is "you may not see this", drawn apart from "this read failed": it says so and offers no retry.

teamIndexView.about: The header of the teams page and its create-team dialog: three tabs (find / mine / pending) and a "Create team" button, with the middle column left to a child route; the dialog holds avatar, name, address and intro. Where the tabs go, that column's content and the create request all live in the container `teams/Index.vue`.

s1.name: The header and three tabs
s1.note: Default state: the three tabs and the "Create team" button on the right, with the middle column empty (the catalog has no child route).

s2.name: The create dialog, open
s2.note: After tapping "Create team": avatar, name, address (prefixed with the current host) and the intro editor are all there, and the primary button is "Create team".

s3.name: The create is in flight
s3.note: After submitting: the primary button spins and cannot be pressed, and the dialog stays open so nobody presses it again thinking it did not register.

s4.name: The name is taken
s4.note: The duplicate-name error sits under the name field; the dialog and everything typed stay.

s5.name: The address is taken
s5.note: Same for a taken address: the error sits under the address field, and the person just edits the address.

teamMembersView.about: The Members section of team settings: an Invite button beside the title, then four cards (how people join, join requests, members, sent invitations; requests and invitations only when there are some) and an invite dialog. Reads and writes live in the container `teams/detail/Members.vue`.

s1.name: Members
s1.note: One row per person, each with a role chip and a line on what the role can do. Promote, demote and remove sit in the row menu; a member the server will not let you remove has no menu.

s2.name: Join requests
s2.note: A pending request: who, their message, when; reject and approve on the right; the card title counts what is still waiting.

s3.name: Sent invitations
s3.note: An invitation still waiting: who, when, and a Withdraw button.

s4.name: The members tab could not load
s4.note: The list did not come back: this tab turns into the failure state, states the reason and offers a retry, rather than drawing "No members".

s5.name: Requests still loading
s5.note: A spinner in the card; it does not say there are none.

s6.name: The invite dialog found someone
s6.note: Whoever the username or email lookup found is laid out first: avatar, name, username. That is who gets invited, visible before the button is pressed.

s7.name: That person is already in the team
s7.note: The same person is already a member: the dialog says so, and "Invite" is greyed out.

teamJoinLinkCard.about: How people join, in the Members section: the long-lived team link (copy, reset), whether joining needs approval, and who can find the team. The team address lives in Profile. Reads and writes are in the container `teams/detail/Members.vue`.

s1.name: The link is back
s1.note: The default: a read-only link with copy and reset beside it; below, the approval switch and the two visibility choices, each with a line under it.

s2.name: Just copied
s2.note: After pressing copy: the button's label becomes "Copied", so nobody presses it again thinking it did not register.

s3.name: The link is not back yet
s3.note: The link has not arrived: that section is a spinning progress bar, not an empty text field - it says it is loading, not that there is nothing.

s4.name: It did not go through
s4.note: A read or write failed: a red bar states the reason, the rest of the card stays as it was, and the person can try again.

adminCiActivityPageView.about: The CI and merge queue screen: how long PRs wait in the merge queue, how long jobs wait for a runner, how long CI required takes, and how long each job and step takes on each runner.

s1.name: Two days of data
s1.note: The default: the first day had no merge, so its queue median is empty and the line breaks there; below are the runners and the slowest jobs.

s2.name: A job's steps expanded
s2.note: One self-hosted runner picked and the e2e row expanded: p50, p90 and longest per step, and a dash for a step with no samples.

s3.name: Backfilling, last sweep stopped by quota
s3.note: A new deployment's first day: the header says how far back the data reaches and how many runs' jobs are still unread, and quotes why the last sweep stopped.

s4.name: Could not load
s4.note: No board was ever fetched: the page shows only that line and a retry.

sleepOff.name: No AI teammates working, sleep prevention off
sleepOff.note: The list of working AI teammates is empty and the switch is off. The computer can sleep when idle.

teamAgentPicker.name: Choose a team connection
teamAgentPicker.note: Choose a connection, an available model, and the device that will execute tasks.
teamAgentPicker.about: AI teammates in project settings choose a team connection, one of its models, and an execution device.

assistantPanel.about: The app's one Cheese panel, held by the app shell; its header just says Cheese. Each step of a turn is one line, folded into one when the answer is done; what it wrote into a draft is a card where every field can be undone; a message or task it drafted for the person is a card waiting for them, which they can edit and only then send; things left for the person to confirm and published results are cards too. Earlier topics sit above, set apart by New topic.

s1.name: Publish page, nothing asked yet
s1.note: An empty conversation: one line on what it can do, a few starters below, and a button to add files beside the box.

s2.name: Writing a draft
s2.note: Cheese has read the file and looked through the space's tasks, and is filling in the task: the last step spins.

s3.name: A finished turn
s3.note: The steps fold into one line; the deadline in the changes card was undone (struck through); a 'Needs your check' card; the published result offers 'View task'.

s4.name: Three tasks from one file
s4.note: A file handed over with nothing typed. The first task fills the open draft and is listed field by field; the other two are new drafts, one line each, opened by their names.

s5.name: Earlier topics
s5.note: What was said before New topic sits above, to read only; Earlier topics reads further back. On desktop the panel can be pinned to the right or unpinned.

s6.name: Drafting in a project
s6.note: Asked in a channel what needs the person: Cheese read the history and drafted a reply (waiting, editable, with Send and Set aside) and a task (already opened, with View).

s7.name: A routine's run
s7.note: A conversation the platform started: the line on top says the routine started. Cheese drafted a reply; you were away, so the card waits for you. The card the last run left has expired.

s8.name: A memory saved
s8.note: Cheese notes something about you; a Memory card appears in the panel and can be undone

s9.name: A long piece of work under way
s9.note: The checklist sits on top, ticked as it goes; words and steps appear in the order they happened; of two subagents one is working and one is done, and opening one lists its steps.

s10.name: A long piece of work done
s10.note: The checklist folds to one line, both subagents are done, and words and steps keep the order they happened in.

s11.name: Saying more while Cheese works
s11.note: While Cheese answers, + and the microphone stay; typing or picking a file turns the button into send, and it goes into the answer under way.

s12.name: Work done, nothing written
s12.note: The answer says Cheese gave no answer; earlier messages of the topic are read back with Earlier messages.

s13.name: With the page, a selection and citations
s13.note: The row in the box: the page Cheese reads and the text selected this time, the same chips as attachments. The last question's cited document and task are chips, with one line each under it: the selection, and the page it was asked on.

s14.name: Page left out
s14.note: The page's × clicked: the name is struck through and × becomes +, which brings it back; the next page is included again.

s15.name: Citing with {'@'}
s15.note: Type {'@'} in the box and the menu opens above it; the pick becomes a chip in the box.

myDraftsView.about: My drafts: tasks not yet published in this space, and unsaved changes to published ones. Open one by its name; deleting asks first.

s1.name: A few drafts
s1.note: Two new tasks and one set of changes, marked as such; the source names the imported file.

s2.name: None
s2.note: After the last one is deleted.

spaceLibraryView.about: The space's Library page in the sidebar: members see files open to all members; admins see both tiers. Clicking a row previews it on the right; admins upload from the header and change visibility or remove from each row's ⋯ menu.

s1.name: Admin
s1.note: Four files, each row showing who uploaded it, when and its size; the admins-only file carries a tag.

s2.name: Member
s2.note: No upload button and no admins-only files; the ⋯ menu only offers Download.

s3.name: One file open
s3.note: The text file previews in the right pane. Admins also see its download count and how many guidance settings list it.

s4.name: Nothing yet
s4.note: Says “No files yet” and draws no search box.

s5.name: Still loading
s5.note: A spinner in place, not “No files yet” first.

s6.name: One file open on a phone
s6.note: The file fills the page with Download at the bottom; the top bar's ← returns to the list.

s7.name: Upload dialog
s7.note: Pick a file, then who can see it; each choice says who that is. Upload stays disabled until a file is chosen.

settingsAssistantView.about: The Cheese page in settings: the lists of what needs and needs no confirmation (checked kinds plus your own entries), automations (one list: when, what, its state; repeating ones can be viewed, paused, resumed and deleted, a waiting one-off cancelled, and a one-off leaves the list once it has run), and recent actions (done or asked, with the reason when asked).

s1.name: With routines
s1.note: Three routines: one on a schedule, one that runs when someone {'@'}-mentions you and left 1 action to confirm, one paused because credits ran out.

s2.name: Nothing set yet
s2.note: No entries of your own, so “No confirmation needed” says None; no routines.

citeMenu.about: The menu {'@'} opens in Cheese's box: pick a task, channel, document, library file or problem to cite as a chip. Each row says on the right which project and channel it is in.

s1.name: Just typed {'@'}
s1.note: Recent places first, then the four kinds in this project; click one to list that kind.

s2.name: Typed a few letters
s2.note: Grouped by kind, at most 4 each, the project in view first; the matched letters in bold.

s3.name: Five already cited
s3.note: A question cites at most 5 things; typing {'@'} again only says so.

versionsView.about: Task detail 'Version history' tab: each version's number, time, author, what changed, and the files it held. Whether they download is the server's to say.

s1.name: Three versions, newest on top
s1.note: Default cell: version 3 is marked current; a draft deleted later keeps only its name in version 2; version 1's files were not recorded.

s2.name: Opened from a project
s2.note: The address carries ?version=2: version 2 is marked and scrolled to.

s3.name: Someone who has not started the task
s3.note: Sees every version and file name, with no download button and a note that files download once they start.

agentRules.about: When Cheese makes or changes an automation, the answer carries a card: when, in bold; what it does; and a line with its state and the one thing to do (cancel a wait, pause one that is on, resume a paused one). When a one-off fires, the platform says what happened in the same conversation and Cheese carries on.

s1.name: Just made
s1.note: Waiting once for a task to go to review: the card says Waiting, with Cancel. Nothing over the input.

s2.name: After it happened
s2.note: The card says Started; the platform line says the task went to review, and Cheese answers below.

s3.name: Card states
s3.note: Waiting, started, cancelled, gave up after 14 days, a repeating one that is on, one paused for credits. Ended cards are grey and have no button.
